title: Moderate Prenatal Cadmium Exposure and Adverse Birth Outcomes: a Role for Sex-Specific Differences?
ehr_evidence: The sample was derived from the ALSPAC study, a population-based study investigating environmental and genetic influences on the health, behaviour, and development of children.
summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between moderate prenatal cadmium exposure (maternal blood Cd) and birth outcomes, with a focus on sex-specific effects.
key_findings: Maternal blood Cd was adversely associated with birthweight (unstandardized B coefficient -62.7 g, 95% CI -107.0, -18.4) and crown-heel length (-0.28 cm, 95% CI -0.48, -0.07) in adjusted regression models.

Stratified by sex, maternal blood Cd was adversely associated with birthweight (-87.1 g, 95% CI -144.8, -29.4), head circumference (-0.22 cm, 95% CI -0.39, -0.04), and crown-heel length (-0.44 cm, 95% CI -0.71, -0.18) in girls but not in boys.
No significant association was found between maternal blood Cd and low birthweight or preterm delivery.
Maternal blood Cd did not mediate the association between smoking and birth outcomes.
data_source_type: Primary cohort study with biospecimen analysis and questionnaire data
population: Pregnant women and their singleton live-born infants from the ALSPAC cohort in the UK (n=4191)
exposure_domain: Prenatal cadmium exposure (maternal blood cadmium levels)
limitations: Potential unmeasured confounders such as other environmental pollutants
Large number of cadmium values below limit of detection affecting continuous variable modeling
